The proxy core answered with HTTP %1$d.
A probe address that follows the default changes with the fallback groups\' test address in Core settings > Group testing.
Lowest delay, fallback and load-balance groups
The lowest delay, fallback and load-balance groups of “%1$s” are generated again, and the rules and apps use them by their targets. The adaptive group goes.
One adaptive group: each connection uses the member expected to work fastest on the current network

“%1$s” becomes one adaptive group, “%2$s”: each connection uses the member expected to work fastest on the current network, and tries the next one in parallel when that pays. Its lowest delay, fallback and load-balance groups are no longer generated; the rules and apps that use them use the adaptive group.
The address the group measures its members with: an https address gets one TLS handshake, an http address one HEAD request.

For each new connection an adaptive group uses the member with the lowest expected time to a working connection on the network the phone is on, from each member\'s success rate and time to the first byte measured on the connections that go through it. When the first choice may fail, the next member is tried at the same time and the first to answer is kept. Each network keeps its own statistics; a group nothing uses sends nothing.
Members, in the order they are tried
Members on %1$s, in the order they are tried

After this time a failure counts half on the fast scale of a member\'s reliability: shorter, the group follows a member that starts failing more often sooner. Failures in a row are a loss window and move the group at once, whatever this is.
How much lower another member\'s expected time must be before the group switches to it. A burst of failures raises the current member\'s expected time at once, so it moves the group anyway.

While the group is in use, a member not measured on the current network for this long is measured with one TLS handshake (a few kilobytes); a member that would be used first if it worked again is measured every reaction time, every half of it while it is in a loss window. 0: never. A group nothing uses never probes.

What a second connection is worth in waiting time. The next member is tried in parallel only when the time it is expected to save reaches this value: 0 tries in parallel whenever it can help, a larger value less often.

After this time a failure counts half on the slow scale, a member\'s long-run reliability: shorter, old failures stop counting sooner. A member left for a loss window comes back only once it answers again, not after a time. At least the reaction time.
The longest one attempt is waited for. Each member\'s own deadline follows from its measured times and stays below this.
How adaptive groups choose, try in parallel and measure

These values reach every adaptive group. A change is applied with the configuration; the statistics the groups learned are kept. A custom group becomes adaptive on its own page (Rules > Custom groups).

Every connection of this group then uses “%1$s” only, on every network: no choice by expected time, no parallel attempt, no probe. The statistics keep being updated, and the automatic choice can be restored at any time.
Lowest expected time on this network
Kept: no other member is %1$d%% faster
Every other member is failing: the last resort is tried alongside
Nothing measured on this network yet: in configuration order
Time to the first byte of each member on this network, counted in the statistics
